Subject: Dedicated reservation options for SableBridge

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We need a concrete set of dedicated reservation options to review with our infrastructure and procurement teams. Key asks: cluster size (GPU count) ranges, minimum guaranteed GPUs, ramp cadence (weeks/months), and what warm-start / prewarm credits we get during early months.

Our initial workload profile: interactive chat + nightly batch embedding jobs. Peak steady-state target is ~600 concurrent chat tokens/s with occasional batch embedding windows. We care about predictable tail latency (95th < 150ms) and also unit cost visibility.

Can you send 2–3 proposal lanes (pilot -> scale) and a recommended default for a conservative launch? Ideally show activation windows and burn expectations month-over-month.

I attached a short intake form with our rough QPS and retention requirements. Procurement copied here: procurement@sablebridge.com.

Thanks,

Liam — thanks, this is clear. High level, I outlined three lanes below with activation/ramp and minimums. I included expected burn cadence and a recommendation based on your profile (chat + nightly batch). I also attached a draft offer PDF with the same tables.

Summary lanes (illustrative; final pricing in attached PDF):

1) Pilot Lane — "Warmstart"
- Initial cluster: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 4 (soft floor)
- Ramp: 4w stabilization -> add 4 GPUs at week 5 if 95th latency or throughput targets met
- Use case: dev + limited production; low upfront commitment; can convert to Production lane after month 2
- Warm-start credits: 150k tokens-worth of warm cache pre-population (one-time)

2) Production Lane — "Anchor" (recommended conservative default)
- Initial cluster: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 12 (hard floor)
- Ramp: staged over 12 weeks: +6 GPUs at week 4, +6 GPUs at week 8
- Use case: sustained interactive traffic + nightly batches; keeps 95th latency headroom
- Warm-start credits: higher priority prewarm and KV cache persistence during activation windows

3) Scale Lane — "Slate"
- Initial cluster: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs (or split across two zones for geo failover)
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 24 (hard floor)
- Ramp: 3-month runway with monthly add-ons based on utilization thresholds
- Use case: aggressive growth and bursty embedding pipelines

Operational notes and controls:
- Smart routing: requests can be routed off-hosted fallback pool if anchor capacity is saturated (auto-fallback policy)
- Autoscale and burst: autoscale up to double committed capacity during scheduled burst windows; burst rate subject to billing tier
- Activation window: we recommend a 2-week warmup window prior to go-live to populate KV cache and tune kernels for your sequence mix

Recommended pick: Production Lane with a soft early-stage floor (start 24g, degrade to min 12g for planned maintenance) — gives room for batch loads while keeping cost predictable. If you prefer lower near-term spend, the Pilot Lane is the safe fast-onramp.

Next steps:
- I can convert the attached draft into a purchase-ready DocuSign.
- Proposed call Thursday 8/21 to walk through SLA exceptions and activation timing.
